To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of information technology in pricing decisions is associated with lower price rigidity; and (2) this effect is moderated by the extent to which the firm is able to implement the IT-based pricing system.

(i) information technology is an important determinant of price rigidity, (ii) price rigidity is a function of firm size and the level of information technology use in an industry, (iii) price rigidity in an industry is a function of industry size and the level and sophistication of information technology use, and (iv) the relationship between price rigidity and information technology is moderated by the level of competition in an industry.

(a) firms can use technology to reduce the costs of price adjustment, and (b) this can lead firms to be more price flexible, but only if they also have a greater ability to monitor their markets and to react to price changes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of technology on the process of price setting in firms.
the role of information technology in the digital economy, and the implications for the pricing processes and strategies that firms adopt in the presence of IT-enabled price flexibility.

the role of information technology as a facilitator of strategic pricing in business operations.
Should we expect less Price rigidity in the Digital Economy? (2003)
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we should expect less price rigity in the digital economy.

the digital economy will not lead to less price rigidity, but it will lead to more price flexibility, and this is the result of the new technology that allows firms to implement dynamic pricing strategies.
the digital economy has not yet changed the way firms set prices, but it has changed the way they can implement prices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new framework for understanding the impact of information technology on pricing processes.
information technology can be expected to reduce price rigidity in a firm's product market.

we have shown how the use of information technology can be a source of price rigidity in firms and industries, as well as a source of price flexibility, and that the net effect on the economy as a wholes depends on the relative importance of these effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of technology for price management is likely to have a profound impact on the way in which firms set and adjust prices, and on the extent of price rigidity in firms.
the use of technology to manage price is not a simple, one-dimensional process.
we can expect to see a significant decline in the rigidity of prices in firms, industries, and the economy as information technology continues to evolve.
